entries.rationale: The printed equations use plasma concentrations while declaring Y as Plasma or Lymph. This implementation evaluates association and dissociation with concentrations in the named local compartment. This is a disclosed locality interpretation; the author control stream has not been checked.
entries.conservation_implications: The binding contribution cancels in antibody plus complex and target plus complex for either convention. That stoichiometric cancellation does not certify whole-body conservation, physical dimensions or positivity. A plasma-driven lymph reaction can consume local species without local reactant availability.
entries.qualification_limits: A literal printed-plasma reconstruction and a local-lymph reconstruction represent distinct source conventions. Neither is rejected as scientifically incorrect solely for this choice. Complete author-code, dimensional and whole-body conservation qualification remain open.

models.limitations: Lymph binding uses local lymph coordinates rather than the plasma coordinates printed in supplementary equations 134-136 (page 32). This disclosed source interpretation is archive-bound in source_interpretations; author-code and physical-unit qualification remain open. BBB and BCSFB reflection inputs are separate for AAV vector and proteins. sigma_vector_bbb and sigma_vector_bcsfb affect AAV equations; sigma_protein_bbb and sigma_protein_bcsfb affect mAb, TargetX and their complex together. A protein-only perturbation leaves all vector equation coefficients unchanged. A shared perturbation must explicitly set both vector and protein inputs and therefore affects AAV, mAb, TargetX and complex. All four coefficients use unit 1, values from 0 through 1 and the retained source numerical scale. The protein profile deliberately groups mAb, TargetX and complex at their disclosed common barrier defaults; a TargetX-only perturbation is not represented. Other organ reflection, interstitial/CSF reflection, diffusion, receptor and transgene coordinates are unchanged. Complete source, author-code, physical-unit and whole-body conservation qualification remain open.
